tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — VERY SHORT BRISTLY COMBS
tiles.details: On ONE attached flowering culm count usually 6–8(–10) short, one-sided bristly branches near the upper axis. A full culm and 1-cm scale are needed to distinguish these from the longer combs of blue or hairy grama; existing target photo supports the gross fuzzy-head clue, not a measured count.
tiles.short: Several ~1-cm flowering branches, not long grama eyebrows
tiles.status: FIELD CUE VISIBLE; SCALED FULL CULM NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTED TUFT AND TRUE HAIR LIGULE
tiles.details: Published Kew description: caespitose perennial, flowering culms approximately 10–50 cm, narrow blades about 1–2 mm wide. Expose the INNER blade–sheath junction to see the short hair-fringe ligule; no reliable species-specific ligule length is established here. Do not call marginal blade hairs a ligule or infer a rhizome from a cropped head.
tiles.short: Small perennial tuft; short fringe of hairs at the inner collar

tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT A SINGLE MATURE SPIKELET
tiles.details: An intact one-sided branch carries several laterally compressed spikelets. In one ripe 2.5–4 mm spikelet, identify the lower bisexual fertile floret and the reduced upper sterile floret. Measure the body separately from projecting awns. This anatomy is not resolved in the existing whole-head photos.
tiles.short: Spikelet body about 2.5–4 mm; fertile plus reduced sterile floret

tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE BOTH GLUMES
tiles.details: Kew GrassBase describes one-veined lower and upper glumes; the upper may be ciliate on its keel, two-toothed at the apex, and have its OWN ~1–2.5 mm awn. Photograph each glume with its attachment and 1-mm scale. Do not confuse an upper-glume awn with an awn arising from either lemma.
tiles.short: Lower ~2–3.5 mm; upper ~2.5–4 mm and itself short-awned

tiles.heading: 05 · TWO LEMMAS, DIFFERENT AWN LENGTHS
tiles.details: Published fertile lemma body ~2.5–4 mm, with three relatively short awns (central ~1.5–2 mm; laterals ~1 mm). The reduced upper sterile lemma is also three-awned, often with much longer ~5–10 mm awns. A fuzzy branch may show many awns from DIFFERENT florets: count them only after dissecting one mature spikelet and tracing their insertion.
tiles.short: Fertile lemma 3-awned; reduced sterile lemma has longer awns

tiles.heading: 06 · TEXAS GRAMA OR LOOK-ALIKE?
tiles.details: Sideoats grama has many short branches down a much longer central axis; blue grama usually 1–3 longer curved eyebrows; hairy grama only a few longer densely spikeleted combs, often with a distal bare extension; red grama has slender appressed units. Use matched mature branches and a dissected spikelet. Existing comparison panels depict OTHER species, not rigidiseta anatomy. Keep Bouteloua sp. if branch and lemma characters cannot be resolved.
tiles.short: Very short bristly branches versus sideoats, blue, hairy and red gramas
tiles.status: COMPARISON LESSON — MATCHED SCALED PHOTOS NEEDED

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: Find the VERY SHORT fuzzy or bristly flowering branches, often several (approximately 5–9) near the upper axis rather than one or two broad eyebrows. Each branch carries awned spikelets, giving a small tufted or starburst appearance. It is NOT enough to see 'a fuzzy grass' — photograph one entire culm and then the narrow hairy branch close up.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Start with Joey Santore's same-species photograph and the existing two arrows on visible flowering clusters. The other locally stored Glass Root Garden photo carries only private-study permission and must NOT be treated as a cleared public-gallery photograph.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Published Kew description: caespitose perennial, flowering culms approximately 10–50 cm, narrow blades about 1–2 mm wide. Expose the INNER blade–sheath junction to see the short hair-fringe ligule; no reliable species-specific ligule length is established here. Do not call marginal blade hairs a ligule or infer a rhizome from a cropped head.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: An intact one-sided branch carries several laterally compressed spikelets. In one ripe 2.5–4 mm spikelet, identify the lower bisexual fertile floret and the reduced upper sterile floret. Measure the body separately from projecting awns. This anatomy is not resolved in the existing whole-head photos.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: B. rigidiseta typically has several (often about 5–9) SHORT bristly/awned units near the top. Blue grama has only about 1–3 long curved combs. Sideoats grama carries many short pendant oats down a much longer axis. Red grama has narrower, more appressed, often purplish branches and awned spikelets; color alone is not sufficient. If an entire culm/branch cannot be resolved, keep Bouteloua sp.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

memory_rule: Photograph ONE complete seed-bearing culm to show several SHORT clustered units toward its top; do not count units from neighboring stems in the photo.
safety_note: Do not claim microscopic glumes/ligule/awn count from these macroscopic views. Taxon IDs follow recorded source determination; native status unchanged.
